correctness.rationale: At each Fisher triangle, either three external edges are matched or one is matched and the other sockets are paired. When two matchings differ at a triangle the two changed sockets are linked by either one internal edge or a two-edge path; hence alternating-cycle components correspond bijectively to the cycle components in the difference of even base subgraphs. In the given binary coordinates, a difference with b=1 selects one horizontal edge per sector, with rungs exactly at switches, making one connected cycle. With b=0 a single proper run gives a cycle, separate runs give separate cycles, and all ones gives two rim cycles, not one. An independent planar-dual argument confirms this: the dual is the suspension of C_n by two nonadjacent poles, and simple primal cycles correspond to bonds. Opposite pole colors make both sides of the cut connected regardless of the equatorial colors. Equal pole colors give a bond iff the other color occupies one nonempty proper interval; the whole equator in the other color would disconnect the poles. This yields the join for every n≥3, including the triangular prism. There are cross-part two-step paths and a nonedge inside each part (complementing all coordinates), so the diameter is exactly two. Counting the interval generators gives the stated degree, edge count and distance distribution.
residual_risks: Independent finite replay checks the base cycle-space geometry only, not the entire expanded graph; the written local triangle argument establishes the exact lift. No restriction to bounded-length flips is allowed in this result.

evidence: Ciucu–Liu–Yang give the bijection with even subgraphs and 2^{|E|−|V|+1} matchings for cubic Fisher graphs.

Bošković's clique-decoration theorem applies (all original degrees equal three and the cliques are triangles), giving connectivity and a bound on the permitted length of each flip; his separately named Fisher decoration uses a different gadget.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The known clique-decoration flip theorem implies connectivity on this family, but does not give the complete edge set or an upper bound of two on the number of moves. Its cycle-length bound must not be mistaken for an exchange-graph diameter.

evidence: The known count and cycle number yield state count, degree, and hence edge count after the local flip correspondence. Taking all bonds organized by equal or unequal pole colors gives the stronger all-pairs criterion, which is not given by the inspected aggregate cycle counts or general connectivity theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The metric claim and full join are not a renaming of the formulas for counts and do not follow from connectivity with bounded flip lengths; the characterization of the cut generators by their pole/interval pattern is the substantive extra step.

evidence: The local lift identifies the flip graph with the Cayley graph of the binary cycle space on simple cycles, or equivalently the dual dipyramid cut space generated by bonds. OEIS A077265 names the dual-bond equivalence and gives the number of generators.
Ito et al. define the same unrestricted one-alternating-cycle exchange, but study general shortest reconfiguration, not this exact graph.
Resultary 8e7090802d17 treats only designated square flips on unexpanded prisms and Möbius ladders; 3c0b6086f905 treats four-cycle flips on K_n×K_2.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The aliases materially overlap in move model or cycle counts, but neither designated-square models nor the aggregate bond count determine the interval-join adjacency. Duality supplies an alternative reduction and exposes the needed structural partition by pole colors.

originality.rationale: The Fisher bijection and state count are prior. The exact generator count, hence regular degree once one identifies flips with base cycles, is also prior in a different formulation: OEIS A077265 counts prism cycles (equivalently dipyramid bonds) by exactly 2^n+n(n−1). The distinct contribution supported here is the classification of all adjacency by the interval-Cayley join and the resulting uniform sharp two-flip distance, not the raw counts or general connectivity.
residual_risks: A structural characterization of dipyramid bonds or a stronger cut-space distance result in unindexed material might cover the join; bounded searches and the inspected aggregate formula do not establish global priority.

value.rationale: The join determines every legal move in an exponentially large matching space and gives an explicit at-most-two-move routing rule independent of n. That structural information is useful and distinct from the old counts; the uniform sharp metric conclusion does not depend on estimates for the length of each move.
residual_risks: No mixing-rate or short-cycle-only routing conclusion follows.
